A1.justification: Both supplied PDFs contain 11 readable pages of the same DiffusionGS paper, supporting comparison of text, equations, figures and tables. Both end with references; neither contains appendix pages.

before.justification: v4 reports original object-generation and scene-reconstruction experiments, a 25-participant user study, and component ablations in Section 4 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v5 retains the original benchmark results, user-study outcomes and ablations in Section 4 and Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical Gaussian prediction and rendering procedures, denoiser architecture, mixed training, RPPC conditioning, dual decoders, losses and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain Objaverse, MVImgNet, RealEstate10K and DL3DV10K training, ABO/GSO and RealEstate10K benchmark evaluation, and the same real-camera, wild-image and generated-image demonstrations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in every corresponding experiment in Table 1 and Figures 6–8. This includes the same object-generation baselines, scene methods, and PhotoNVS comparison with post-hoc Gaussian fitting.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains identical preprocessing, splits, metrics, training budgets and resolutions, and one input view plus ten testing views per instance. The user study still involves 25 people, 14 objects and a 1–6 scoring scale.

E4.justification: Section 4.2, Table 2 and Figures 8–9 retain the same component ablations, mixed-training and RPPC analyses, and generation-diversity examples.

E5.justification: The random-seed variation used to illustrate diversity in Figure 9(b) is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals, error bars or significance tests for the quantitative benchmarks.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 contain identical results, including DiffusionGS PSNR/FID of 25.89/9.03 on ABO and 21.63/15.87 on RealEstate10K. User-study scores, runtimes, ablation values and qualitative outputs also match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), the RPPC definition, its translation-invariance statement and the mathematical reasoning in Section 3 are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about single-stage Gaussian diffusion, mixed training, RPPC, view consistency and accuracy/speed advantages.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning occlusion handling, mixed-training benefits, RPPC depth perception and limitations of post-hoc Gaussian fitting are unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: The preprocessing instructions, optimizer, numerical precision, GPU counts, iteration budgets and resolution schedule are identical. The project-page access information and its hyperlink are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, research-positioning passages and all 91 references are unchanged; no cited work or novelty relationship is added or removed.

P1.justification: The only visible textual edit is the page-1 arXiv stamp, changing from v4 dated 26 Jun 2025 to v5 dated 11 Oct 2025. Manuscript wording, title, authors and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9, Tables 1–2, captions and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages match apart from the updated arXiv stamp text on page 1.

improvement.justification: Only the arXiv version/date identification changes. Identical scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and document presentation leave the paper's overall quality unchanged.
